transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um, well, I'm here because I've started catching myself thinking that it would just be easier if I didn't wake up. And sometimes, like on the drive home from school, I start wondering if my family and my students would be better off without me. It really scares me to think like that, because I don't want to actually act on it... but it's happening enough that I knew I needed to come in and talk to someone.
Have you noticed any changes in your interest or enjoyment in activities that you used to find pleasurable, like hobbies, time with family, or teaching?

Yeah, I definitely have. Um, I used to really look forward to things like my softball league, my book club, working in my garden... and even the robotics club I run at school. But lately, I just kind of go through the motions. Or I just cancel altogether. It's like none of it really feels enjoyable to me anymore.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately, like eating a lot less or more than usual?

Yeah, I have actually. Most school days, I just... I forget to eat, or I avoid eating until late in the afternoon. And over the past year, my clothes have gotten noticeably looser. I'm not trying to lose weight at all, it's just happening.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or like you’re a burden to others, even when there’s no clear reason for it?

Yes, I do. Um, especially at work. If a lesson goes badly, or even if a student just looks confused, I immediately take it as proof that I’m letting everyone down. I end up just replaying it in my head over and over. It makes me feel like I’m a terrible teacher, and... well, it makes me feel like I'm a terrible mother, too. I just constantly feel like I'm failing everyone.
Have you noticed that you're moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, that you can't sit still and feel restless or agitated?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I don't feel like I'm moving in slow motion, and I'm not feeling restless or jittery either. I'm just... tired, mostly. But my actual movements and how I talk seem pretty normal to me.
Can you tell me if these feelings of depression and loss of interest have been present for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at a time?

I'm honestly not sure if it's been exactly like that. I haven't really kept track of the days. Um... it definitely feels like things have been hard for a while, but I don't know if I could say it's been most of the day, every single day for two weeks straight. I just haven't noticed if it's been that constant.
Can you tell me if there have been times when you felt down or hopeless for at least two weeks straight, without any real break in those feelings?

Um, like I was just saying, I really haven't been keeping track of the exact timeframe. It definitely feels like I've been down for a while, but... I don't know if I can say for sure that it's been two solid weeks without a single break. I just haven't been paying close enough attention to the calendar to know if it's been that continuous.
Can you think of a specific two-week period where you felt down or hopeless most days, without much of a break?

I know we're kind of going over the same thing, but... no, I really can't pinpoint a specific two-week block for you. Like I said, I don't keep a journal or track my moods on a calendar. The days just sort of blur together lately. I know things have been hard for a while, but I just can't say for sure if there was a specific fourteen-day stretch with absolutely no breaks. I just don't have that exact of a timeline for you.

Can you think back to when these feelings of being down, losing interest in things, and feeling like a burden started? Was there a time when these feelings lasted for at least two weeks without a meaningful break, even if you couldn't mark it on a calendar at the time?

Well, when you put it like that, asking when it all started... I can give you a better idea of the timeline. It's been going on for about a year and seven months. It started right around the time I took over the STEM assessment redesign at school, which was on top of my regular teaching load. So, while I can't give you a specific two-week block, I know this whole feeling has been hanging over me since then.
Can you tell me if there was a time when you felt down, lost interest in things, and felt like a burden for at least two weeks straight, without any meaningful improvement during that time?

I feel like we're kind of stuck on this two-week thing, and I really don't have a different answer for you. Like I just said, it's been a year and seven months of feeling this way. Have I felt down and like a burden that whole time? Yes, pretty much. But I honestly don't know if there was a specific fourteen-day stretch where I didn't have a single moment of improvement. I just don't remember my days that specifically to give you a definite yes or no.

Can you tell me if there was a time when you felt down, lost interest in things, and felt like a burden for at least two weeks without any meaningful improvement during that time, even if you can’t recall the exact dates?

I... I really don't know how else to explain it. We keep coming back to this same question about the two weeks. 

Like I said, I've been feeling this way for over a year and a half. But if you need me to say, for a fact, that there was a fourteen-day stretch where I didn't have a single okay day or any meaningful improvement at all... I just don't know. I really can't give you a definite yes or no to that specific question.

Can you think back to whether there was any time during the past year and a half when these feelings came on more strongly and lasted for at least two weeks without letting up, even if you can't remember the exact dates?

I feel like we're just going in circles here. I really don't know how else to answer this. I can't tell you if there was a time it came on stronger and lasted exactly two weeks. It's just been a constant, heavy feeling for the last year and seven months. I don't track it that closely. I just know it's always there.

Can you recall if there was ever a time when your mood was so low that it affected your ability to function normally — like taking care of your kids, teaching, or doing chores — and it lasted for a couple of weeks or more without much relief?

Yeah, it definitely affects how I function. I mean, at work... I’m really falling behind on my grading and lesson planning, and it's getting to the point where it's actually affecting my classroom. I made a grading mistake recently that honestly scared me a bit, just because I always used to be so meticulous about that kind of stuff. 

And outside of school... I’ve pretty much stopped showing up for my friends and family the way I used to. It feels like most of my life right now has just narrowed down to barely getting through the school day, and then going home completely exhausted.

Can you tell me if there was a clear period when your mood was so low that it significantly interfered with your ability to function — like teaching, grading, or taking care of your family — and it lasted for at least two weeks without much relief?

I feel like I'm just repeating myself, but... I really can't say if there was a specific two-week block where it was suddenly worse. It's just been this way for a year and a half. The struggling at work, the exhaustion... it's just how my life is now. I don't know how to break it down into a clear two-week period for you.

Can you think back to whether there was ever a time when your mood was so low that it significantly interfered with your ability to function — like teaching, grading, or taking care of your family — for at least two weeks straight without much relief?

I really don't know how else to say this... I feel like you keep asking me the exact same question. I don't have a specific two weeks to give you. It's just been a constant struggle for the last year and seven months. It hasn't let up.
